display_name: Montes Alpha M, Valle de Colchagua
raw_content:
{
  "hook": "Colchagua's foothills deliver the heat needed to ripen Cabernet Sauvignon fully, resulting in a dense, dark profile. This bottling sits at the top of the producer's pyramid, demanding oak integration before release.",
  "wine_summary": "This wine matters because it put Chilean premium wine on the map during the 1990s boom. Montes established themselves early by focusing on cool-climate sites within warm regions to maintain balance. The wine consistently delivers power without losing structure, distinguishing it from cheaper valley floor bottlings.",
  "terroir_expression": "Across the Apalta sector, granitic soils mixed with clay dominate the landscape, forcing vines to dig deep for water. High diurnal temperature shifts preserve acidity despite the latitude. You taste this in the black fruit core backed by fresh tension rather than jammy sweetness.",
  "vinification_summary": "Building structure requires extended maceration to extract color and tannin after fermentation in stainless steel. Aging takes place in new French oak barrels for roughly eighteen months, softening the grip. Malolactic fermentation converts sharp malic acid into softer lactic acid, rounding out the mid-palate.",
  "food_pairing": "Order lamb shoulder slow-roasted with rosemary to use fat for softening tannins. Smoked brisket with charred edges matches the oak treatment perfectly. Hard aged Manchego stands up to the alcohol warmth without clashing. Mushroom risotto with truffle oil echoes the earthy undertones. Grilled ribeye with chimichurri highlights the black fruit.",
  "comparable_wines": "Clos Apalta — same Apalta vineyard source but Carmenere dominant. Catena Zapata Malbec Argentino — similar high-altitude structure from the Andes. Caymus Special Selection — comparable ripe fruit profile from a warm climate.",
  "style_profile": "Full-bodied dry red with structured tannins and concentrated dark fruit",
  "cellar_recommendation": "Young vintages need air to open up properly. Bottles from 2018 onwards will evolve positively through 2035.",
  "value_assessment": "$75 to $110 positions this against entry-level Napa Cabernet. You pay less here than for Silver Oak or Caymus while getting similar concentration. The 2018 vintage at $105 offers better integration than the current release.",
  "market_position": "Restaurant lists feature this as a premium New World option for steakhouse patrons. Collectors seek older vintages to track evolution over time. Casual drinkers might find the tannins too firm without decanting.",
  "insider_take": "Too often buyers open this bottle young and mistake youth for harshness. Let the 2021 vintage sit for at least three years before uncorking. Skip this if you prefer lighter, earth-driven styles over power.",
  "aging_potential_years": 15,
  "drinking_window_min_years": 2,
  "drinking_window_max_years": 12,
